# KEYS management guidance versus actuals

As of 2026-10-19. Independent primary-source evidence; no canonical portfolio files edited.

## Conclusion
All 11 consecutive quarters from Q1 FY2024 through Q3 FY2026 exceeded the upper end of the immediately preceding earnings-release revenue and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance. There were no misses against those original one-quarter ranges. This is evidence of consistent near-term execution and/or conservative range-setting, not proof of reliable longer-term demand forecasting. FY2024 still had a substantial revenue/EPS contraction, and the two largest tax/tariff-related EPS distortions require adjustment.

Revenue is USD millions, EPS USD/share. Actual revenue uses the consolidated statement rather than rounded billion-dollar headlines. Dates and direct URLs are provided in guidance_vs_actual.csv and .json. A beat means above the original upper bound, not above analyst consensus. No exhaustive inter-quarter update search was completed; absence of an interim revision is NOT established. Original prior-quarter ranges are preserved rather than replaced by later outcomes.

## Preliminary versus audited results
The table deliberately scores original release-time actuals against the original prior-quarter guide. The parent research team reports that the FY2025 audited 10-K subsequently shows net income $850m and GAAP EPS $4.91, versus preliminary release $846m/$4.89. The archived release consolidated revenue is $5,375m (its headline rounds to $5.37bn), not $5,374m. Annual audited revisions should be reconciled separately; do not substitute audited annual figures into this quarterly release-time scorecard. The parent team holds the audited filing and is responsible for that reconciliation.

## Comparability / quality of beats
- Q3 FY2024: EPS $1.57 includes a $0.16 tax-rate change benefit ($0.11 relating to the first half; $0.05 to Q3). Management disclosed $1.41 excluding that change, still $0.05 above the $1.36 guidance high. The modeled non-GAAP tax rate fell from 17% to 14%. This is not all operating outperformance.
- Q2 FY2026: reported revenue $1,717m and EPS $2.87 include IEEPA tariff refunds and customer-surcharge refunds: revenue reduced about $40m, costs/expenses reduced $97m. Management disclosed ex-one-time revenue $1,758m and EPS $2.58, versus original $1,690–1,710m/$2.27–2.33. Both still beat; normalized EPS beat high is $0.25 instead of $0.54. Do not annualize reported 72.3% gross margin. Ex-one-time gross margin was 67.6%. Q1's original outlook explicitly excluded consequences of the tariff court decision.
- Q4 FY2025 reported revenue included $11m from recently closed acquisitions and $7m positive FX; full-year growth was 8% reported, 7% core. FY2026 acquisitions and currency add to reported growth: Q1 growth 23% includes eight acquisition points and one FX point. Distinguish organic/core execution from purchased revenue.
- ESI annual renewals make Q1 unusually strong (40–45% of its annual revenue historically recognized in Keysight Q1); comparisons with pre-ESI seasonality can mislead.

## Longer-horizon guidance and revisions
These are management's own scenarios/expectations, not analyst forecasts. No claim that they constitute formal full-year ranges.
- [Q4-FY2023 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2023/q4/transcript/Q4-FY2023-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2023-11-20: FY2024 first-half demand expected mixed; management was watching for second-half recovery. ESI included about $60m in initial Q1 revenue guidance. This is a cautious baseline, not a promise of strong recovery.
- [Q1-FY2024 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2024/q1/transcript/Q1-FY2024-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2024-02-20: explicitly stopped assuming a strong FY2024 second-half recovery. Base case: revenue flat Q2-to-Q3, then mid-single-digit sequential growth in Q4, and second-half orders above first half. Actual revenue 1,216 → 1,217 → 1,287m broadly matched this shape (+0.1%, +5.8%).
- [Q2-FY2024 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2024/q2/transcript/Q2-FY2024-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2024-05-20: maintained that stable-Q2-to-Q3 / modest second-half-orders scenario. This was a reaffirmation of the February base case.
- [Q3-FY2024 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2024/q3/transcript/Q3-FY2024-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2024-08-20: expected the year to finish slightly better than anticipated, while cutting the ongoing non-GAAP tax rate to 14%.
- [Q4-FY2024 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2024/q4/transcript/Q4-FY2024-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2024-11-19: initial FY2025 base case revenue growth at the low end of the 5–7% long-term target and EPS growth near 10%; assumed gradual recovery absent further macro deterioration.
- [Q1-FY2025 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2025/q1/transcript/Q1-FY2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2025-02-25: reaffirmed approximately 5% FY2025 revenue growth and 10% EPS growth despite potential US policy uncertainty.
- [Q2-FY2025 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_financials/2025/q2/Q2-FY2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2025-05-20: raised FY2025 revenue growth to midpoint of 5–7% (about 6%), and EPS growth slightly above 10%. Estimated annual tariff exposure $75–100m; Q3 expected greatest impact, with mitigation by fiscal year-end at prevailing tariff rates.
- [Q3-FY2025 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2025/q3/transcript/Q3-FY2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2025-08-19: raised FY2025 outlook to about 7% revenue growth and 13% EPS growth. August tariffs added estimated $75m annual exposure; expected April tariff mitigation by Q1 and August tariff mitigation in first half FY2026. Actual FY2025 growth was roughly 8% revenue / 14% EPS.
- [Q4-FY2025 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2025/q4/transcript/Q4-FY2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2025-11-24: initial FY2026 revenue growth excluding acquisitions at/above 7%, $375m acquisition revenue, EPS growth at/above 10% despite mild acquisition dilution. Accelerated expected August-tariff mitigation into Q1. Acquisition synergies targeted above $100m.
- [Q1-FY2026 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/Q1-FY2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2026-02-23: raised FY2026 total revenue and earnings growth expectation to just above 20%. Maintained $375m acquisition-revenue expectation and >$100m synergies, weighted late in year.
- [Q2-FY2026 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/transcript/Q2-FY2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2026-05-19: raised FY2026 revenue growth to high-20s, with typical sequential Q4 increase; maintained $375m acquired revenue and >$100m synergies. Raised capex expectation to around $200m.
- [Q3-FY2026 prepared remarks](https://s22.q4cdn.com/444849635/files/content_files/Q3-FY2026-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): 2026-08-18: Q4 revenue $1,930–1,950m and EPS $3.34–3.40 imply about 32% FY2026 revenue growth and 60% EPS growth at midpoint. Integration largely complete a quarter early; 80–90% of $100m cost synergies expected as exit-year run rate. These FY2026/Q4 outcomes remain unresolved as of this research date.

## Management assessment and underlying drivers
Assessment: strong operational delivery and credible evidence of improving demand, with important cyclicality and adjustment caveats. Conservative short-term guide ranges have been exceeded through downturn and recovery. The FY2026 upward revisions are supported by orders and core revenue, not just acquisitions: Q3 orders $2,091m, +52% core; revenue $1,846m, +31% core. But growth forecasts rose sharply as evidence arrived, so do not interpret eleven quarterly beats as precision in forecasting inflection timing.

- AI infrastructure: Q3 FY2026 remarks describe wireline orders more than doubling, with AI scale-out, speed transitions, silicon photonics and system-level emulation as four demand sources. Wireline revenue exceeded wireless for the first time. This supports technical complexity/design intensity as a driver; it also increases reliance on AI investment momentum.
- Diversification: Q4 FY2025 remarks identify defense modernization, non-terrestrial networks, 5G Release 18/19 and early 6G, general electronics, leading-edge semiconductor and photonics. Q3 FY2026 reported CSG +43% and EISG +21%. These are management-attributed drivers rather than independent customer-spend verification.
- Downcycle realism: Q1/Q2 FY2024 remarks documented cautious customer spending, foundry construction/production delays, and constrained manufacturing spending. The eventual flat-Q2/Q3 revenue pattern supports the revised scenario; it does not erase the decline versus FY2023.
- Costs/integration: Q3 FY2026 operating margin 33.2% exceeded the 31–32% long-term target, with core 34.7%. Earlier integration/synergies support improvement, but cost synergies and exceptional operating leverage should not be extrapolated indefinitely.
- Risks to monitor: tariffs and refund accounting; geopolitical/trade restrictions; customer capex and R&D budget cyclicality; factory construction timing; acquisition integration and EPS dilution; software revenue timing; tax adjustments; and the distinction between backlog conversion and sustainable new orders. These are analytical monitoring priorities grounded in the cited commentary, not a quantified probability forecast.

## Sources and auditability
- All 12 original IR release HTML files and plain-text extractions are archived locally. Source URL and byte counts: source_manifest.json. These include Q4 FY2023 to establish Q1 FY2024's original guidance.
- All quarterly prepared-remarks PDFs from Q4 FY2023 through Q3 FY2026 were downloaded from Keysight's official CDN, linked by its official events page. PDF/text pairs and remarks_manifest.json preserve sources. Three earlier FY2023 PDFs were also collected for context.
- Exact guide/actual source dates and URLs appear in the CSV/JSON. Table uses primary releases, not consensus databases.
- Limitations: no exhaustive interim-release, Q&A, customer or competitor cross-check; no independent interviews reviewed. Prepared remarks are management's controlled communications. The official quarterly-index page rendered incompletely, so the official past-events page supplied PDF links. Python urllib returned 403, while ordinary curl downloads succeeded; no authentication or access restriction was bypassed. Raw release HTML includes navigation and scripts, so use the extracted values and corresponding original tables for verification.
